solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Short time for booze?

parts.note: Clare Short was a Labour MP and cabinet minister, so her first name stands in for her surname
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A quick pint before closing: is there a short time left for a drink?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short time' reads as a brief spell, but Short is the politician Clare Short, whose first name is the piece wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is red Bordeaux wine, which is one kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Town bird's penetrated by one

indicators.note: something penetrated has another thing pushed inside it, so the bird's letters surround the other piece

parts.note: a lark is a songbird
an means one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: A town where some bird has been penetrated by somebody: a lurid local news story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird's' reads as a possessive, but it stands for 'bird is', and one is the article rather than the digit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanark is a historic market town in South Lanarkshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Course for forgetful students about to put on more lippy?

indicators.note: putting one thing on another sets the two side by side, the first placed ahead of the second

parts.note: re is Latin for concerning or about
fresh means cheeky or impudent, so fresher is cheekier; lippy is British slang for cheeky

explanation.surface: Students who keep forgetting things are about to put on more lipstick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lippy' looks like lipstick to be put on, but here it is the adjective for cheeky, and 'more' makes it comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher course revises knowledge people have let slip, so it suits students who have forgotten.

clue.text: (& 26dn.) Miliband, in shit, badly wants spot on TV, which speechifying minister stands by

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the politician's name is placed within the rude word
something done badly is botched and jumbled, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a spot or small area is a patch
Ed Miliband was Labour leader at the time
the box is British slang for the television

explanation.surface: Ed Miliband, in trouble, is desperate for a slot on television, as the Commons speaker looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: ED goes into SHIT and the six letters are then mixed. The dispatch box is the lectern-like box in the House of Commons from which ministers make speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministers stand beside the dispatch box on the Commons table when addressing the House, so it is where they deliver speeches.

clue.text: Skimpy top causes boner, then shaft

indicators.note: then signals that one piece follows directly after another in sequence

parts.note: a boner is a blunder, and so is a boob
a shaft or hollow cylinder is a tube

explanation.surface: A revealing top provokes an arousal, and then something further: smutty Private Eye innuendo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boner' is meant to raise a smirk, but it is the old word for a gaffe.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob tube is a strapless, tight-fitting tube of fabric worn round the chest, a famously skimpy garment.

clue.text: A waxing process that's a bit messy on end of prick

indicators.note: in an across or down reading, one piece placed on another follows it
something messy is disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A painful waxing treatment gets a little messy at the tip of something delicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waxing' suggests hair removal, but batik is a way of dyeing cloth using wax.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is an Indonesian textile technique where wax resists dye on parts of the fabric.

clue.text: see 19ac.
Boob by arse-over-tip House of Commons — "just a small one"

indicators.note: by means beside, so the second piece is placed next to the first

parts.note: boob and tit are both slang for a breast

indicators.note: arse over tip means head over heels, turned upside down, so the letters are flipped in order

parts.note: HC is the abbreviation for House of Commons

explanation.surface: A Commons sex scandal: someone tumbles over and insists it was just a small one.
explanation.walkthrough: Titch is British slang for a small person; the down reading turns HC upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A titch is an informal term for a tiny person or thing, hence a small one.

clue.text: Snoop hard at it getting stiff

parts.note: someone hard at work is busy
a stiff is slang for a corpse, a dead body

explanation.surface: A nosy parker caught in the act and getting aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' looks like an innuendo adjective; it is the noun for a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody meddles in other people's affairs, just as a snoop pries into them.

clue.text: Really being before Tories' no. 1 is nice? Eff-off!

indicators.note: before places the anagram in front of the remaining piece
food that is off has gone bad, so these letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: number one is the first in line, so only the initial letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the party name

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the Tory leader is really nice and gets a sweary brush-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eff-off' reads as a censored curse, but it splits into the fodder EFF and the anagram signal 'off'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In effect' means in practice or in reality, the same sense as really used as a sentence adverb.

clue.text: Does it give you an objective feel for sex?

definitions.text: Does it give you an objective feel for sex?

parts.words: Does it give you an objective feel for sex?
parts.note: surface reading: a question about getting an impartial, detached view of sex
setter's reading: a sexual feeling directed at an object, such as shoes or rubber

explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' looks like impartial, but it means object-centred: arousal by a thing rather than a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is sexual attraction focused on an inanimate object or a non-genital body part.

clue.text: We hear our posh Eye contributor's O.B.N. candidate

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken version, so the sound rather than the spelling counts

parts.note: Slicker writes Private Eye's City column; 'our' in a cut-glass accent comes out as 'ah'

explanation.surface: Private Eye is talking about its own upper-class columnist being up for an award.
explanation.walkthrough: The O.B.N., Order of the Brown Nose, is Private Eye's mock honour for toadying; Slicker is the pen name of its financial columnist.
explanation.definitionFit: The magazine awards its Brown Nose to the most fawning sycophants, so a crawler is a natural nominee.

clue.text: Routinely approve of Johnny mounting Frank?

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece mounting another sits on top of it, so it comes first

parts.note: johnny and rubber are both British slang for a condom
to frank a letter is to stamp it

explanation.surface: Someone casually approves of a man called Johnny having sex with a man called Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnny and Frank pose as men's names; both are ordinary words here.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubber-stamp is to give automatic official approval without real scrutiny.

clue.text: Chef's support round bum

parts.note: a hob is the cooktop on which a chef rests pans
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A chef's backing for a plump backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' looks like the British word for bottom, but it is the American word for a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is a homeless vagrant, which is the American sense of a bum.

clue.text: Trashy personal housing publicity

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the run of letters is held within the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Tabloid gossip pages giving trashy personal stories publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is extravagant promotional publicity designed to whip up interest.

clue.text: Withdrawal of the main bidet — be prepared!

indicators.note: something prepared has been made up or worked into shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A bathroom being stripped of its main bidet, with the scout motto shouted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic term for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An ebb tide is the falling tide, when the sea draws back from the shore.

clue.text: Wee Kate worried by a disclosure

indicators.note: something worried is agitated and shaken about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written
a leak is an unauthorised disclosure of information

explanation.surface: A little Kate is upset by a revelation about her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like the Scottish word for small, describing Kate; it is the verb for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a leak is slang for urinating, which is what wee means as a verb.

clue.text: "Wayward, ecstasy-gobbling Di, no nun" slur

indicators.note: gobbling swallows something whole, so the drug's letter is taken inside the other words
wayward means wilful and straying, so these letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A tabloid jibe that Princess Di, pill-popping and wayward, was no nun.
explanation.walkthrough: Di is Princess Diana; the quoted remark is itself the kind of slur the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect, insinuating remark, usually disparaging, so it is a veiled slur.

clue.text: Whopper nut hurt badly

indicators.note: something put together badly is botched, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A huge lump on the head left someone's nut hurt badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whopper' suggests something big, as a bump might be, but here it is slang for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A whopper is a gross lie, and an untruth is a falsehood.

clue.text: (& 6dn.) Act like wanker Archer, briefly, entertaining film company

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests holds them within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Jeffrey Archer, the novelist and disgraced Tory peer, known for short by the pet form of his first name
RKO Radio Pictures was a Hollywood studio

explanation.surface: Jeffrey Archer, briefly hosting a film studio, behaves like a tosser.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go JE, then RKO, then FF. Wanker is British slang for a contemptible person, and also for someone who masturbates.
explanation.definitionFit: To jerk off is slang for masturbating, which is literally what a wanker does.

clue.text: Name Dave's first entry into chump Boris's place

indicators.note: making an entry into something means going inside it, so the pair sits within the fool

parts.note: a loon is a fool or crazy person
N is the abbreviation for name

indicators.note: first keeps only the opening letter of the name

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: David Cameron's first foray into the patch of a buffoon called Boris.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson was then Mayor of London, so his place is the city he ran.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson governed the capital as its mayor, so the city he ran is his place.

clue.text: You won't score if you get one, dear

definitions.text: You won't score if you get one
definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, a batter out without scoring a run has made nought
second meaning: a term of endearment, especially in the north of England

explanation.surface: A sympathetic warning to someone hoping to pull: you won't get anywhere, dear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests sexual success, but it is runs in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A duck is the cricket term for a nought, and 'duck' is a regional affectionate address like love or darling.

clue.text: Australian's boob lifted with energy for money

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the letter for energy is added after the other piece
in a down entry, lifting something raises it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: nork is Australian slang for a woman's breast
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An Aussie woman has a breast lift, paying with energy rather than cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Nork is Australian slang, unfamiliar to many solvers; read upward it gives KRON.
explanation.definitionFit: The krone is the currency of Denmark and Norway, so it is a form of money.

clue.text: Peak time to get pissed with the drink issue

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the following pieces are joined on in sequence

parts.note: high means intoxicated, as is pissed in British slang
the drink is slang for the sea
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: The best time to get drunk, with the booze question still unresolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' looks like alcohol following 'pissed'; it is slang for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: High season is the busiest, most expensive part of the tourist year, its peak period.

clue.text: Stabbed in the back, maybe, US election loser style?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pierced by a bull's horn, which might catch someone from behind
second meaning: treated as Al Gore was, read as his name made into a verb

explanation.surface: A politician betrayed in the manner of the man who lost the 2000 US presidential race.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Gore lost the disputed 2000 election to George W Bush; adding -ED makes his name a verb, which many felt described being stabbed in the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Gored means wounded by a horn or tusk, and the pun reads it as having been done over like Al Gore.

clue.text: Yentob, chucking away capital to secure media chief put in grave situation

indicators.note: throwing away the capital means discarding the first letter of the name
securing something means holding it fast within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: Alan Yentob, the BBC executive, without his first letter
the leading letter of the word

explanation.surface: BBC grandee Alan Yentob, shedding money, ends up in a grave situation over a media boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Yentob was a long-serving BBC executive; 'grave situation' is a pun on a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place a body in a tomb, literally putting it in a grave.

clue.text: see 4dn.
More than one arsehole produces tears round organ

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to rend is to tear
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A gang of jerks causing tears in someone's insides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' reads as weeping, but it is the verb meaning rips; the second piece sits after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rear ends are backsides, so more than one arse, though here the clue uses the coarser word.

clue.text: Balls, possibly after syphilis (ale mixture injected), cut down

indicators.note: a mixture blends ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new order
after places the politician's name behind the disease
something injected is pushed inside, so these letters go within the disease

parts.note: the pox is an old name for syphilis
anagram fodder
Ed Balls, the Labour shadow chancellor, is one possible Ed

explanation.surface: A man's testicles, struck by venereal disease after a mixed drink, have to be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' poses as testicles, but it is the politician Ed Balls, with 'possibly' admitting he is one example of an Ed.
explanation.definitionFit: To poleaxe someone is to fell them with a heavy blow, so poleaxed means knocked or cut down.

clue.text: Heaving with an erection backed by ruler

indicators.note: by means beside, so the ruler is set next to the first piece
something backed is moved backwards, so its letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: a man with an erection is said to be up
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch, aroused, heaving with passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heaving' suggests panting passion; it means retching.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaving is retching or trying to vomit, and puking is vomiting.
